_comment: Recording of live run 35 (status done); the plan is the model's own words.

steps.message: Reviewing the intake and the question.

claims.text: The goal is a 30% cut in electricity bought from the grid by 2030 at P.S. 236 Langston Hughes (1871 Walton Avenue, Bronx) on an $800,000 capital budget. Rooftop solar alone is only about 22% to 24% of annual use and does not reach the goal by itself.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: Efficiency only (Scenario A) is estimated to cut about 6% to 18% of annual use. It fits the budget but does not reach the 30% goal.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: Efficiency plus the whole-roof solar array (Scenario B) is estimated to cut about 28% to 42% of annual use, within budget. The low end falls just short of 30%, so it is not certain to reach the goal.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: The full path (Scenario C: deeper efficiency, the whole-roof array and a backup battery) is the only scenario whose low end clears the goal, at about 31% to 46% of annual use. Its typical cost range runs up to $283,593 more than the $800,000 budget, so meeting the goal may take more than the amount set aside. Whether to extend the budget is the owner's decision once the gap is compared with the savings.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: The roof is 20 years old or more and the owning agency rates it Not Solar Ready. None of the cost totals include repairing or replacing the roof, so a roofer's quote is needed before solar is committed.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: The intake describes an elementary school of 43,760 sq ft built in 1994, with a flat roof of 10,260 sq ft, served by Con Edison, with a capital budget of $800,000 for 2027.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: Existing systems: the intake lists no existing solar or other renewables and no efficiency work already done. The plan therefore assumes none. Please confirm, because completed work such as LED lighting would lower the efficiency savings.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: Annual grid electricity of 456,834 kWh (kilowatt-hours, energy over time) matches the figure in the city's 2024 Local Law 84 energy report. It is treated as measured. The baseline for the goal is the electricity the building buys from the grid.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: The city's tax-lot record lists the address as 1869 Walton Avenue and a gross floor area of 46,700 sq ft, against 43,760 sq ft entered in the intake and in the energy report. The 43,760 sq ft figure is kept as the working figure. Please confirm the floor area.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: City building outlines show one building with a ground footprint of 10,255 sq ft, close to the 10,260 sq ft roof area entered. A footprint is not a measured roof, so roof area still needs to be verified by an engineer or roofer.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: The city record shows no landmark flag. The Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) current flood map puts the address in zone X, an area of minimal flood hazard.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: Usable roof is 55% of the roof area, after setbacks and obstructions (roof setback factor 0.55).
claims.label: ASSUMPTION

claims.text: The array needs 66 sq ft of usable roof for each kW (how much power at one moment) of panels.
claims.label: ASSUMPTION

claims.text: System losses of 18% (low) to 10% (high) around the solar tool's 14% default; weather is typical-year data.
claims.label: ASSUMPTION

claims.text: Efficiency measures (LED and controls) save 10-20% of annual use. This is a planning estimate, not a cited benchmark and not a building model.
claims.label: ASSUMPTION

claims.text: Critical load was not given, so it is estimated at 1.0 W per sq ft x 43,760 sq ft = 43.8 kW (a planning estimate, not metered). Backup length was not given, so 8 hours is assumed. Battery energy = kW x hours / 0.85 round-trip efficiency = 412 kWh.
claims.label: ASSUMPTION

claims.text: Planning-level benchmark prices, not quotes: solar, battery and efficiency prices come from completed NYC projects (NYSERDA data). Efficiency savings of 10-20% (standard) and 15-25% (deep) are planning estimates, and only 62%-88% of them is counted because the City's audited projects delivered that share.
claims.label: ASSUMPTION

claims.text: The city's 2024 energy report shows site EUI (energy use per square foot) of 57.6 kBtu (thousand BTU) per sq ft and an ENERGY STAR score of 69.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: The same report shows natural gas of 893,000 kBtu and fuel oil of 69,276 kBtu, so heating is largely non-electric. Heating fuel is outside an electricity-use goal and is not counted in the 30% target.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: A standard efficiency package (such as LED lighting and controls) is estimated to cut about 28,300 to 80,400 kWh a year, or 6% to 18% of use. Only 62% to 88% of the predicted savings is counted, because the City's own audited projects delivered that share. The underlying 10-20% savings figure is a planning estimate, not a building model.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: The intake does not say what lighting, controls or cooling the school has. Before pricing, an energy audit should confirm what is already installed, because existing LED lighting would lower these savings.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Usable roof is about 5,643 sq ft after setbacks (10,260 sq ft x 0.55). The roof area is the user's number and should be verified.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: The whole usable roof fits an array of about 85.5 kW DC.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: The array is modeled at about 101,100 to 111,100 kWh a year (middle value about 106,100 kWh), for a flat roof with a 10 degree tilt facing south. System losses of 18% (low) to 10% (high) around a 14% default; weather is typical-year data.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: That output equals about 23% of annual use (middle value). Rooftop solar alone does not reach the 30% goal.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: Solar bill savings are about $20,028 to $26,864 a year, using the New York commercial average price of 19.8 to 24.2 cents per kWh. This is the state average, not this building's own tariff.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: The owning agency's own assessment rates the roof Not Solar Ready, in fair condition and 20 years old or more. The roof should be checked, and replacement considered, before solar goes on it.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: Scenario A (efficiency only): cuts about 6.2% to 17.6% of annual use, which is 21% to 59% of the goal. It does not reach the goal.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: Scenario A cost: typical range $80,174 to $275,471 upfront; the median of similar NYC projects is about $175,424. Net cost is the same, with no incentive counted. Simple payback is about 4 to 49 years (median about 14), which is not the full SAM model. It fits within the budget and gives no backup power in an outage.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: Scenario B (efficiency plus solar within budget): cuts about 28.3% to 41.9% of annual use, which is 94% to 140% of the goal. The low end is just under 30%, so it does not reliably reach the goal.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: Scenario B cost: typical range $347,875 to $674,585 upfront; the median is about $487,585. Net cost after the federal credit is $267,565 to $554,851 (median about $393,937). Simple payback is about 5.8 to 21.6 years (median about 11), not the full SAM model. It fits within the budget (43% to 84% of it). It gives no backup power: solar panels shut off in an outage without a battery.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: Scenario C (deep efficiency, whole-roof solar and a backup battery): cuts about 31.4% to 46.3% of annual use, which is 105% to 154% of the goal. It reaches the goal even at the low end.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: Scenario C cost: typical range $592,242 to $1,083,593 upfront; the median is about $822,708. Net cost after the federal credit is $444,447 to $863,495 (median about $644,146). Simple payback is about 8.7 to 30.4 years (median about 16), not the full SAM model.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: Budget: Scenario C reaches the goal, but its estimated cost is up to $283,593 more than the budget. Reaching the goal may take more than the amount set aside; compare that gap with the savings before deciding whether to extend it. At the low end it fits (74% of the budget); at the high end it is 135%.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: Outage backup: Scenario C is sized for about 8.0 to 9.4 hours on the critical loads. Scenarios A and B give no backup.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: The model treats the $800,000 capital budget as one total upfront figure. The roof is not modeled for repair or replacement.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: Scenario C itemized, expanded efficiency package: typical range $99,590 to $349,935; median of similar NYC projects about $227,503. About 91,367 kWh saved a year (15-25% planning estimate) times $1.09 to $3.83 per kWh saved, from completed NYC public-sector projects (NYSERDA data).
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: Scenario C itemized, rooftop solar: typical range $267,700 to $399,114; median about $312,160. 85.5 kW DC at $3,131 to $4,668 per kW, the middle half of 558 completed NYC non-residential projects of 25-100 kW since 2022 (NYSERDA data).
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: Scenario C itemized, backup battery: typical range $224,952 to $334,544; median about $283,044. 412 kWh at $546 to $812 per kWh, the middle half of 56 completed or approved NYC commercial-scale storage projects (NYSERDA data).
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: Federal credit counted in net cost: 30% of solar and battery, about $147,796 to $220,097 (median about $178,561). Governmental entities can receive the credit as a direct payment, and the program page shows it open, with solar required to be placed in service by 2027-12-31. Whether this school or agency qualifies is not confirmed, so net cost may be higher if it does not.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: The NYSERDA NY-Sun commercial solar incentive is uncertain: its current block status could not be read from the official page. It is left out of net cost. Check the dashboard in a browser.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: The NYC Solar Schools program (DCAS, NYPA, NYC Public Schools) has put solar on 130 schools under power purchase agreements. Whether this building is in the pipeline is unknown, so the program is uncertain and left out of net cost. Ask DCAS or the SCA.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: Local Laws 92 and 94 of 2019 are a rule, not an incentive: if the roof undergoes certain major renovations, it must carry solar, a green roof, or both. A roof replacement before solar could trigger this rule.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: The cost totals leave out roof repair or replacement. A roofer's quote is needed.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Phase 0, confirm data and budget: gather 12 months of Con Edison bills, confirm the budget year (2027) and that $800,000 is one capital total, confirm floor area, existing systems and the building's own tariff.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Phase 1, professional reviews: a licensed professional engineer (PE) or registered architect (RA) must do the structural analysis, and a roofer must do a roof condition survey and price any repair or replacement. The roof cannot be certified from these records.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Phase 2, efficiency measures: commission an energy audit and install the efficiency package first (lighting and controls not already in place). It is the lowest-cost step and lowers the load that solar and battery must cover.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Phase 3, permits and Con Edison interconnection application: use a licensed electrician, get FDNY rooftop access approval, and submit the Con Edison interconnection application. Work through the Department of Education approval route (DCAS, NYC Public Schools or the SCA).
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Phase 4, solar installation: install the roughly 85 kW array once the roof is cleared. To keep the federal credit available, the solar must be placed in service by 2027-12-31, so schedule reviews early.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Phase 5, battery, commissioning and verification: add the battery sized from confirmed critical loads, commission the system and compare 12 months of bills against the estimates.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Scenario C gives about 8.0 to 9.4 hours of backup for the critical loads named in the intake: emergency lighting and communications.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: Scenarios A and B give no backup power. Solar panels shut off in an outage without a battery.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: Critical load not given, so estimated at 1.0 W per sq ft x 43,760 sq ft = 43.8 kW (a planning estimate, not metered). Backup length not given, so 8 hours is assumed. Battery energy = kW x hours / 0.85 round-trip efficiency = 412 kWh. Provide a metered critical load and desired backup hours to resize.
claims.label: ASSUMPTION

claims.text: FEMA's current map shows flood zone X (minimal flood hazard), so no flood-zone protection is triggered by this reading. The 2015 preliminary map was not checked, and NYC code uses the more restrictive map. Heat and winter-storm ratings were not looked up.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: A licensed PE or RA must do the structural analysis. This plan cannot certify that the roof can hold panels.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: A roof condition survey is needed: the roof is 20 years or more old and rated Not Solar Ready.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: A licensed electrician, FDNY rooftop access review and a Con Edison utility interconnection review are required before installation.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: The building is a Department of Education school. The approval route runs through DCAS, NYC Public Schools or the SCA. The list at the end of the plan has the links.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: If the roof is replaced or majorly renovated, the sustainable roof rule (Local Laws 92 and 94) may require solar, a green roof, or both. Confirm with the Department of Buildings.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Ask a roofer or engineer to verify the roof area, pitch, direction, structure and shading, and enter the verified figures to re-run the plan.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

sections.title: Path to net-zero and learning resources

claims.text: Net-zero electricity is not reachable from this roof alone: rooftop solar covers about 22% to 24% of annual use. The rest must come from efficiency or other sources.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: Natural gas and fuel oil heating are outside an electricity goal. Replacing them with electric heating would raise electricity use and should be planned separately.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Ask DCAS or the SCA whether this school can join the NYC Solar Schools program, which uses power purchase agreements and could lower the capital needed for solar.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: The year the roof was last replaced is missing from the intake. Roof age comes from the city's solar-readiness record (20 years or more). Confidence in solar sizing is lowered.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: The electricity price is the New York commercial average, not this building's own tariff. The tariff must be confirmed on a bill. Con Edison lists several general-service tariffs (for example SC-2 and SC-9, effective 2025-02-01), and none is chosen here.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: The incentive list is kept by a person and each program page is re-checked by the system. The NY-Sun incentive and NYC Solar Schools status are uncertain and left out of net cost. The federal credit is counted because its page shows it open, but this school's eligibility is not confirmed.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: Only the FEMA flood zone was read. Heat and winter-storm ratings were not checked, and neither was the 2015 preliminary flood map.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: Battery sizing rests on an estimated critical load and assumed 8 hours of backup, so battery cost and outage hours are low confidence.
claims.label: ASSUMPTION

claims.text: The efficiency savings of 10-20% are a planning estimate, not a building model, so every efficiency range is low confidence. Lighting type, controls, cooling type, owning-agency details and a metered critical load were not given.
claims.label: ASSUMPTION

claims.text: Costs are planning-level ranges from completed NYC projects, not quotes. Simple payback is not the full SAM model. Savings are estimates with ranges and are not assured.
claims.label: ASSUMPTION

claims.text: Please confirm: the floor area (43,760 vs 46,700 sq ft on the tax-lot record), roof area, any existing solar or efficiency work, the tariff, and the budget year and type.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

roadmap.footer_note: All figures are planning estimates with ranges. They are not quotes and are not assured. The roof cannot be certified from these records; a licensed PE or RA must do the structural analysis.
